result.note: Tests the hydro projects approved in Arunachal Pradesh: the Lohit basin first, the local benefit-sharing terms and the capacities and flood-moderation budget.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, the Union government approved the 1,200 MW Kalai-II hydroelectric project in Arunachal Pradesh. It is the first hydropower project on which river?
questions.explain: Kalai-II is the first hydropower project on the Lohit river, opening an entirely new basin. It sits in Anjaw, a border district, and is part of India's push to establish prior use across the Brahmaputra system.
questions.source: Kalai-II is the first hydropower project on the Lohit river, opening an entirely new basin.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, the Union government approved the Kamala and Kalai-II hydroelectric projects in Arunachal Pradesh. Consider the following statements about the benefits to the state:
items: Arunachal Pradesh holds a 26% equity stake in the Kamala project.
Arunachal Pradesh receives 12% free power from both plants.
An additional 1% of power is earmarked for a Local Area Development Fund.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct as stated in the approval terms. New Delhi is also funding over 225 km of roads and bridges across the two project sites.
questions.source: Arunachal Pradesh holds a 26% equity stake in the Kamala project and receives 12% free power from both plants, plus an additional 1% earmarked for a Local Area Development Fund.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the hydroelectric projects in Arunachal Pradesh approved in April 2026:
items: Flood moderation component of the Kamala project — INR 40,175 crore
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: The flood moderation component of the Kamala project has a dedicated budget of INR 4,744 crore. INR 40,175 crore is the total approved for both projects. The plants are meant to manage peak demand and steady a grid increasingly reliant on solar and wind.
questions.source: The Kamala project also provides flood moderation in the Brahmaputra Valley, with a dedicated budget of INR 4,744 crore for that component alone.
